offer_letter.markdown:
# Offer of employment — Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst

## 1. Job Offer: Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst

Dear {{employee.full_name}}, We are pleased to offer you the position of Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst at Absa Group. This is a permanent role. Your start date will be 1 December 2026.

## 2. Your Role

You will support Coverage Bankers in managing a portfolio of corporate and institutional clients. Your work will include preparing client briefs, pitch materials, and account plans, tracking client activity and pipeline, and conducting financial statement analysis. You will build financial models, perform credit analysis, support deal execution, and work with teams like Risk, Legal, and Product partners. You will also help with KYC/AML compliance, due diligence, industry research, and sector reports.

## 3. Where and When You Will Work

Your place of work will be Sandton, head office. You will work 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You will take a 60-minute meal break after no more than five hours of work. The first 3 months of your employment will be a probationary period.

## 4. Your Pay

You will earn R18,000.00 per month as your basic salary. This is paid monthly on the 25th by EFT. Deductions for PAYE and UIF (1%) will be made from your pay.

## 5. Next Steps

Please bring your ID and qualifications when you join us. This offer is valid until 30 November 2026. If you have questions, contact us at hr@example.co.za.

## 6. Acceptance

Please sign and date this letter to accept this offer: {{employee.full_name}}, {{date_signed}}.

contract.markdown:
# Contract of employment — Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Sandton (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst. The Employee's duties include: Support Coverage Bankers in managing a portfolio of corporate / institutional clients; Prepare client briefs, pitch materials, and account plans; Track client activity, opportunities, and pipeline; Maintain strong understanding of client strategies, industries, and financial performance; Conduct financial statement analysis (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow); Build and maintain financial models and forecasts; Perform credit analysis and risk assessments; Develop client profitability and return analysis; Assist with execution of lending, advisory, and capital markets transactions; Coordinate internal stakeholders (e.g., Risk, Legal, Product teams); Prepare documentation for deal approvals and credit committees; Support due diligence and data gathering processes; Ensure adherence to KYC / AML requirements; Ensure adherence to internal risk and compliance policies; Assist with regulatory submissions and audit requests where required; Work closely with product partners (e.g.: Corporate Finance, Transaction Banking, Markets, Treasury); Help structure integrated solutions aligned to client needs; Support cross-sell initiatives across the CIB platform; Conduct industry research and competitor analysis; Monitor macroeconomic trends affecting clients; Produce insight reports and sector updates. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Sandton, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This clause names who is entering the contract: Absa Group as the employer, and you as the employee. It also records your ID number and address as part of the agreement.

You are being appointed as a Business Intelligence - Coverage Analyst with a detailed list of duties related to client support, financial analysis, deal execution, and compliance. Your employer can also ask you to do other reasonable tasks that fit with this role.
Your job starts on 1 December 2026. This is a permanent position, meaning it has no fixed end date.

Your first 3 months are a trial period where your employer will check how well you are doing in the job. You will get fair feedback, guidance and support during this time, and any decision to confirm, extend or end your employment after probation must follow a fair process.
You will work at the Sandton head office.

You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, 5 days a week, from Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after working no more than 5 hours straight. You are also entitled to at least 12 hours of rest between workdays and at least 36 hours of rest each week.
Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month, which works out to R103.85 per hour. You will be paid by EFT on the 25th of each month. You will not receive any other cash payments or benefits in kind.

You only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot be more than 10 hours a week. You will be paid 1.5 times your normal hourly rate for overtime, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. Working on a Sunday pays double your normal wage (or 1.5 times if you normally work Sundays), and working on a public holiday pays double your normal wage.
Your employer will deduct PAYE (income tax) and 1% for UIF from your pay. No other deductions will be made unless you agree in writing, or the law, a court, or an arbitration award requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year, to be taken at a time agreed with your employer, and used within 6 months after the leave cycle ends. You get 30 days of paid sick leave over a 3-year cycle, though in your first 6 months you earn 1 day for every 26 days worked; your employer may ask for a doctor's note if you're off for more than 2 days in a row or more than twice in 8 weeks. You are entitled to at least 4 months of maternity leave and 10 consecutive days of parental leave, plus adoption leave as set out by law. After 4 months of employment, if you work at least 4 days a week, you get 3 days of paid family responsibility leave per year.

Either you or your employer can end this contract with written notice: 1 week if you've worked 6 months or less, 2 weeks if you've worked more than 6 months but not more than a year, and 4 weeks if you've worked more than a year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. Your employer can still dismiss you immediately for a serious reason if a fair process is followed, and both parties can agree to skip the notice period.
No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination covers your employer's business, meaning these specific industry rules do not apply to your job.

You must not share or use confidential information about your employer, its clients, or suppliers, whether you're still employed or have left. The only exceptions are if you need the information to do your job or if the law requires you to disclose it.
No other documents are part of this contract besides what is written here.

This contract contains the full agreement between you and your employer, and any changes must be written down and signed by both of you. If any part of this contract gives you less than what the law, a sectoral determination, or a collective agreement requires, the better terms will apply instead. Your employer will keep your employment records for 3 years after you leave and will explain them to you if you ask.
This is the signature section. The employer's signatory signs on behalf of Absa Group, and you sign as the employee, along with the date and place of signing.
